meta.purpose: R-24 and R-25. A single ordered register of every question that must be answered before a defensible decision exists, split into what we know, what we do not know, and exactly how to obtain the missing item. 'How to obtain' is mandatory for every open question because a question without a route to an answer is just anxiety.

answer_state_key.answered: Answered from a Tier 1 source in this session.
answer_state_key.partly-answered: Answered at container level; the trade-area or parcel-level answer is still missing.
answer_state_key.unanswered: No verified answer. Route to obtain it is given.

questions.question: What is the exact expiration date of the lease?
questions.how_to_obtain: Read the term clause in [LEASE-FILE]. Record the date and any extension already exercised.
questions.why_it_matters: Everything — discounting, option windows, the sale window — keys off this.

questions.question: Who is the actual obligor, and is there a guaranty?
questions.known: The brand is Jack in the Box Inc. (NASDAQ: JACK).
questions.how_to_obtain: Read the tenant-identity and guaranty clauses. If a franchisee, obtain its financial statements.
questions.why_it_matters: Determines whether this is investment-grade or speculative credit.

questions.question: Is there a go-dark provision, and may the tenant close and keep paying?
questions.how_to_obtain: Read the operating-covenant clause.
questions.why_it_matters: If yes, a closure does not stop rent but does destroy re-letting leverage at expiry.

questions.question: Does the tenant hold renewal options, and at what rent?
questions.how_to_obtain: Read the option clause.
questions.why_it_matters: An option is a call the owner has written. It caps the renewal case.

questions.question: Does the tenant hold any early-termination right inside 2030-2035?
questions.how_to_obtain: Read the termination clause.
questions.why_it_matters: A termination right is a material defect in the income stream.

questions.question: What is the current annual base rent?
questions.how_to_obtain: Read the rent schedule. Cross-check against the owner's bank deposits.
questions.why_it_matters: The single number without which neither case can be priced.

questions.question: What is the escalation mechanism and what has actually been collected?
questions.how_to_obtain: Read the escalation clause; compare to actual deposits.
questions.why_it_matters: Tests whether the rent has kept real value.

questions.question: What is the owner's adjusted basis and accumulated depreciation?
questions.how_to_obtain: Accountant extracts from depreciation schedules and prior returns.
questions.why_it_matters: Sets the recapture layer and therefore the after-tax number.

questions.question: What is the owner's filing status, other income and residency?
questions.how_to_obtain: Owner supplies to adviser only. Never enters this repository.
questions.why_it_matters: Sets the bracket, the NIIT threshold and the California exposure.

questions.question: Is the owner a passive investor in this asset for NIIT purposes?
questions.known: NIIT is 3.8% and applies to real-estate disposition gains (verified).
questions.how_to_obtain: Adviser determines material-participation status.
questions.why_it_matters: 3.8% of the gain is a real number, not a rounding error.

questions.question: Would the owner actually reinvest under section 1031, and in what?
questions.how_to_obtain: Owner states intent before the sale, not after.
questions.why_it_matters: This single decision can swing the after-tax outcome more than the sale price does.

questions.question: Where exactly is the parcel, and what census tract is it in?
questions.how_to_obtain: Geocode [APN] against the County parcel layer inside the secure workflow.
questions.why_it_matters: Gates every trade-area and hazard lookup.

questions.question: What is the zoning, and what else could the land be used for?
questions.how_to_obtain: ZIMAS parcel report.
questions.why_it_matters: Permitted uses and entitlement constraints inform a reversion scenario and must be considered with the other sale and hold inputs.

questions.question: Is the parcel in a liquefaction, landslide or fault-rupture zone?
questions.known: The region is seismically active; that is not a parcel finding.
questions.how_to_obtain: CGS EQ Zapp by address.
questions.why_it_matters: Drives retrofit cost and rebuild rights.

questions.question: What is the flood zone?
questions.how_to_obtain: FEMA MSC address search, download FIRMette.
questions.why_it_matters: SFHA triggers mandatory insurance and constrains re-letting.

questions.question: What is the fire hazard severity zone?
questions.how_to_obtain: CAL FIRE FHSZ lookup; if LRA, the City's adopted map.
questions.why_it_matters: Rebuild hardening requirements and insurance appetite.

questions.question: What is the building's year built and condition?
questions.how_to_obtain: [SITE-PLAN] plus a commissioned property condition assessment.
questions.why_it_matters: Code vintage sets PML; condition sets reversion value.

questions.question: Can the drive-thru be re-permitted for a different QSR brand?
questions.how_to_obtain: Zoning code plus a pre-application conversation with City Planning.
questions.why_it_matters: Drive-thru capability is the difference between a QSR re-let and a generic retail re-let.

questions.question: What would the market pay today?
questions.how_to_obtain: Three written broker indications, plus recorded comparable transfers from the County recorder.
questions.why_it_matters: Without a price there is no sale case.

questions.question: What spread do buyers apply to a sub-10-year ground lease?
questions.how_to_obtain: Written bid indications and anonymised broker spread data; verify against recorded transfers.
questions.why_it_matters: The dominant valuation input for this asset.

questions.question: Would the tenant itself buy the parcel?
questions.known: The tenant does sale-leasebacks and guided to 'selling real estate' (verified).
questions.how_to_obtain: Ask directly, through the broker, as a priced alternative.
questions.why_it_matters: A tenant buyer can pay more than an investor because it removes its own rent. It is the third path almost nobody prices.

questions.question: Is this unit on the tenant's closure list?
questions.known: 86 closed in FY2025, 38 of them under JACK on Track; 50-100 guided for FY2026.
questions.how_to_obtain: Ask the tenant in writing; check local ABC/licence and closure notices; monitor the County for lease terminations.
questions.why_it_matters: The binary question. If this unit is on the list, hold is not a strategy.

questions.question: How is this unit performing against the system?
questions.known: System same-store sales -4.2% FY2025 and -7.4% in Q4.
questions.how_to_obtain: Request the unit's sales reporting under the lease's reporting clause.
questions.why_it_matters: Rent coverage and renewal appetite both derive from unit sales.

questions.question: Is the franchisee financially sound?
questions.how_to_obtain: Financial statements via the guaranty, or credit report with consent.
questions.why_it_matters: Franchisee failure does not end rent but does start a default-and-re-let cycle.

questions.question: Is the local economy growing?
questions.known: MSA nonfarm employment is +1.29% versus October 2019 and +0.19% versus October 2024. Trade, Transportation and Utilities flat at 0.0%; Information -2.1%; Financial Activities -1.6%; Manufacturing -1.2%. Only Education and Health Services (+3.3%) is clearly growing.
questions.answer: Flat to weakly positive at the container level, with a narrow growth base. Not a growth economy.
questions.how_to_obtain: Already answered at MSA level; still needed at trade-area level (G-10).
questions.why_it_matters: The brief's central premise — 'based upon the existing economic activity in the area' — resolves to this, and it does not support a growth thesis.

questions.question: Is population supporting the trade area?
questions.known: Los Angeles city population fell 0.8% from 2020 to 2025 (verified).
questions.answer: At city level the population is shrinking.
questions.how_to_obtain: Tract-level ACS 5-year for the ring (TA-10).
questions.why_it_matters: QSR volume is a headcount business. A shrinking city is not a headwind you can rent your way out of.

questions.question: Are local incomes keeping pace with the cost of operating a restaurant here?
questions.known: City median household income $81,939 (2024 dollars); poverty 16.5%; fast-food wage floor $20.00/hr; CPI-U +3.7% 12-month.
questions.answer: Incomes are modest against a wage floor that rises automatically and an inflation rate near 4%.
questions.how_to_obtain: Trade-area income distribution (TA-12).
questions.why_it_matters: The operator's margin is squeezed from both ends, which is exactly what produces closures.

questions.question: What is the cost of capital right now?
questions.answer: Verified. Any discount rate must be built as a spread over 4.92%.
questions.how_to_obtain: Already obtained.
questions.why_it_matters: At a 4.92% risk-free rate, the spread a buyer demands on a short-lease QSR is the whole valuation.

questions.question: What happens if the tenant closes this unit and the box goes dark?
questions.known: The tenant is actively closing units.
questions.how_to_obtain: Model it: rent continuation under the lease, retenanting period, TI and leasing cost, and the tax cost of holding a vacant asset.
questions.why_it_matters: This is the base-case downside, not a tail.

questions.question: What does a regional catastrophe do to all three legs simultaneously?
questions.known: The three legs are loss of rent, repairs and exit liquidity, and they are correlated.
questions.how_to_obtain: Run the stress design in data/hazards.json once insurance and PML are known.
questions.why_it_matters: The owner must know the worst case before choosing to hold a single asset in a seismic region.
